inline_comments.comment: Each neo marker function (`only_one_neo`, `zero_or_one_neo`, `one_or_more_neo`, `zero_or_more_neo`) independently calls `configApi.getConfig()` inside its body. This violates the project architectural rule: functions inside `rendering-util/` must not import or call `getConfig()` directly; they must instead receive an explicit `config: MermaidConfig` parameter threaded from the top-level caller. Notably, the existing non-neo counterparts (`only_one`, `zero_or_one`, etc.) never call `getConfig()` at all — they receive only `(elem, type, id)`. The `insertMarkers` call site already knows the current config; pass `strokeWidth` (or the full config) as a fourth parameter to the marker function instead.

`strokeWidth` is destructured from `themeVariables` without a fallback value. If the active theme does not define `strokeWidth`, the template literal `${strokeWidth}` evaluates to the string `"undefined"`, which is an invalid SVG `stroke-width` attribute value and will silently break marker rendering. Add a fallback, e.g. `const { strokeWidth = '1.5' } = themeVariables;` (or whatever the project-standard default is).

All divider lines are unconditionally converted from `rc.line()` to `rc.polygon()` via `lineToPolygon`. The PR description explicitly states only the neo look should use `rc.polygon()`; classic and handDrawn should keep `rc.line()`. For the handDrawn look, roughjs renders a `line` and a near-zero-thickness `polygon` quite differently — the roughness/wobble applied to a polygon with `thickness = 0.0001` will not reproduce the same sketchy aesthetic as `rc.line()`. This is a visual regression for all existing classic and handDrawn ER diagrams. The divider-drawing section should branch on `node.look`: use `rc.polygon()` for `'neo'` and retain `rc.line()` for everything else.

`genColor` only generates CSS color rules when `theme === 'redux-color'`, but `erBox.ts` sets the `data-color-id` attribute for **both** `'redux-color'` and `'redux-dark-color'` (via `COLOR_THEMES = new Set(['redux-color', 'redux-dark-color'])`). Because `genColor` returns `''` for `redux-dark-color`, no CSS rules are ever emitted for those nodes, so the `data-color-id` attribute has no effect and the color-indexing feature is silently broken for the dark variant. Change the guard to cover both: `if (theme !== 'redux-color' && theme !== 'redux-dark-color') { return ''; }`.

The `[data-look=neo].labelBkg` rule has higher CSS specificity than the `.labelBkg` rule defined earlier. For the combination of `redux-color` theme + `neo` look, the `.labelBkg` rule correctly emits `erEdgeLabelBackground`, but the later `[data-look=neo].labelBkg` rule overrides it with `fade(tertiaryColor, 0.5)`, defeating the redux-color-specific background. Either add the same `redux-color` guard here, or restructure so that the neo+redux-color combination gets the correct value.

There are two spaces before `rect` in the CSS selector: `[data-look="${look}"][data-color-id="color-${i}"].node  rect {`. This is likely a typo; use a single space. Also, the closing `}` on the next few lines has an extra leading space (` }` vs `}`), which is inconsistent with the surrounding template.

The new `-pointEnd-margin`, `-pointStart-margin`, `-circleEnd-margin`, `-circleStart-margin`, `-crossEnd-margin`, and `-crossStart-margin` markers are unconditionally appended inside the existing `point()`, `circle()`, and `cross()` functions. These three functions are shared across **all** diagram types that use these marker shapes — not just ER diagrams in neo look. Every diagram that triggers these functions will now create extra DOM marker nodes regardless of look. If these margin-offset variants are only consumed by ER neo rendering, they should be gated (e.g., only appended when `look === 'neo'`) or extracted into dedicated neo-only functions to avoid unnecessary overhead for unrelated diagrams.

`look` and `theme` are top-level config fields, not theme variables. Injecting them via `{ ...config.themeVariables, look: config.look, theme: config.theme }` merges two conceptually distinct namespaces into one object. This works today because `DiagramStylesProvider` types `options` as `any`, but it means styles functions silently depend on fields that aren't part of the canonical theme-variables contract. A cleaner approach is to widen the `DiagramStylesProvider` options type to explicitly include `look` and `theme`, or pass them as separate parameters, so the dependency is visible in the type signature.

Template-literal diagram strings have a trailing newline before the closing backtick (e.g., the last content line is `    CUSTOMER ||--|{ ADDRESS : "has"
` and then the backtick follows on a new line). Per the project's test style convention, the closing backtick should appear immediately after the last content character with no intervening blank line. This applies to all similar template literals throughout this file.

The `data-color-id` attribute is set on `shapeSvg` in two separate places — once in the simple-entity (no-attributes) code path (here, after `drawRect`) and again in the complex-entity (with-attributes) path (~line 241). These are the two branches of the same function. The identical three-line block (`if (theme != null && COLOR_THEMES.has(theme)) { ... }`) is duplicated verbatim. Consider extracting it into a small helper, e.g. `applyColorId(shapeSvg, entityNode, borderColorArray)`, called from both branches.

general_comments.comment: The PR description's **Markers** section states: "New `requirement_arrow_neo` and `requirement_contains_neo` implement neo arrow and contains markers." Neither function appears anywhere in the diff. If these were intended to be part of this PR, they are missing. If they belong to a separate PR, the description should be corrected to avoid confusion during review and future archaeology.

The PR description states: "Optional `colorIndex` is added to `BaseNode` for reuse by other diagrams." However, `BaseNode` in `packages/mermaid/src/rendering-util/types.ts` (line 87) **already declares** `colorIndex?: number` — it was not added by this PR. The field added in `erTypes.ts` to `EntityNode` is still useful for the `node as unknown as EntityNode` cast in `erBox.ts`, but the description is inaccurate and may mislead reviewers into thinking a broader change was made. The PR description (and any related comments) should be corrected.
